normalized.description: Athens International Airport S.A. (hereinafter called “AIA”) acting in compliance with the Airport Development Agreement, as ratified by Law 2338/1995 (Government Gazette A’202/14.09.95), and subsequently amended and ratified by Laws 4594/2019 (Government Gazette Α΄29/19.02.19) and 5080/2024 (Government Gazette A’ 4/ 16.1.2024) is hereby inviting companies and groups of economic operators, including joint ventures / consortia /associations (“Joint Venture(s) / Consortium(a) / Association(s)”) to tender (the “Tenderer(s)”) for the Works identified in the title above, to be executed at Athens International Airport "Eleftherios Venizelos". The respective contract (the “Contract”) will cover all works, services, specific activities, deliverables, and responsibilities required for the design, construction (including structural, civil, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing works), testing, commissioning, supervision, monitoring, operational readiness and handover of Main Terminal Building South Pier expansion and Satellite Terminal Building Western Extension and the associated Apron Works, including all related airside and landside works, utilities, interfaces and all associated systems installations necessary to ensure the proper completion, full functionality, regulatory compliance, and integration with existing airport infrastructure as described in Scope of Works (” SoW”) and the Employer’s Requirements, together with all associated temporary works, logistics arrangements, construction phasing and operational measures required for their safe and timely implementation within a live and fully operational Airport environment. The scope comprises the MTB South Pier Expansion, the STB Western Extension, the associated Apron Works, and a new permanent underground link (bypass tunnel) around the South Pier Expansion. The link will maintain continuous passenger, goods and waste flows between the MTB and the STB during and after construction. The principal Works, described in detail in the SoW, include, without limitation: Approximately 25,000 m² of new South Pier facilities, including contact and bus gates, commercial areas, CIP lounges and support facilities around the South Oculus; Approximately 950 m² of STB Western Extension, providing two (2) new open bus gates, and the conversion of existing Gates C17–C18 into open gate lounges; • Approximately 1,000 m² of reconfiguration works within the existing MTB; • Additional contact aircraft stands; • New Passenger Boarding Bridges, comprising four (4) single and two (2) double bridges, and the rerouting of the existing Passenger Boarding Bridge serving Stands A12/A13; • Construction of a new permanent underground link between the MTB and the STB; • Downgrading, reconfiguration and partial reconstruction of Taxiway P (former Taxiway India) and partial reconstruction of Taxiway E, together with the associated apron and airside infrastructure works; and Realignment of the service road and replacement of the A13 fixed link bridge.

         <cbc:Description languageID="ENG">Athens International Airport S.A. (hereinafter called “AIA”) acting in compliance with the Airport Development Agreement, as ratified by Law 2338/1995 (Government Gazette A’202/14.09.95), and subsequently amended and ratified by Laws 4594/2019 (Government Gazette Α΄29/19.02.19) and 5080/2024 (Government Gazette A’ 4/ 16.1.2024) is hereby inviting companies and groups of economic operators, including joint ventures / consortia /associations (“Joint Venture(s) / Consortium(a) / Association(s)”) to tender (the “Tenderer(s)”) for the Works identified in the title above, to be executed at Athens International Airport "Eleftherios Venizelos".
The respective contract (the “Contract”) will cover all works, services, specific activities, deliverables, and responsibilities required for the design, construction (including structural, civil, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing works), testing, commissioning, supervision, monitoring, operational readiness and handover of Main Terminal Building South Pier expansion and Satellite Terminal Building Western Extension and the associated Apron Works, including all related airside and landside works, utilities, interfaces and all associated systems installations necessary to ensure the proper completion, full functionality, regulatory compliance, and integration with existing airport infrastructure as described in Scope of Works (” SoW”) and the Employer’s Requirements, together with all associated temporary works, logistics arrangements, construction phasing and operational measures required for their safe and timely implementation within a live and fully operational Airport environment.
The scope comprises the MTB South Pier Expansion, the STB Western Extension, the associated Apron Works, and a new permanent underground link (bypass tunnel) around the South Pier Expansion. The link will maintain continuous passenger, goods and waste flows between the MTB and the STB during and after construction.
The principal Works, described in detail in the SoW, include, without limitation:
Approximately 25,000 m² of new South Pier facilities, including contact and bus gates, commercial areas, CIP lounges and support facilities around the
South Oculus;
Approximately 950 m² of STB Western Extension, providing two (2) new open bus gates, and the conversion of existing Gates C17–C18 into open gate lounges;
•	Approximately 1,000 m² of reconfiguration works within the existing MTB;
•	Additional contact aircraft stands;
•	New Passenger Boarding Bridges, comprising four (4) single and two (2) double bridges, and the rerouting of the existing Passenger Boarding Bridge serving Stands A12/A13;
•	Construction of a new permanent underground link between the MTB and the STB;
•	Downgrading, reconfiguration and partial reconstruction of Taxiway P (former Taxiway India) and partial reconstruction of Taxiway E, together with the associated apron and airside infrastructure works; and
Realignment of the service road and replacement of the A13 fixed link bridge.</cbc:Description>

normalized.description: The Contracting Authority is seeking tenders for the procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking. This procurement is being undertaken as part of Phase 2 of Ireland's QCI project (TransEuroOGS), co-funded by the European Commission Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the Irish Department of Culture, Communications, and Sport. The successful tenderer will be required to design, manufacture, and deliver a turnkey telescope unit encompassing the mount, optics, and control software, complying with strict technical and spatial constraints. Key Technical Requirements: Optical Configuration: Ritchey-Chretien (RC) optical design, f/10 to f/12 system, with a clear aperture of at least 700 mm. Low central obstruction is required (30 percent or lower diameter linear obstruction preferred, maximum allowable 34 percent or lower). Optical Coatings and Power Handling: Broad-spectrum reflectivity covering both visible wavelengths and the 1550 nm C-Band NIR telecommunication spectrum, biased for optimal performance at 1550 nm. Reflectance at 1550 nm must be at least 95 percent (protected gold or equivalent high-efficiency NIR coating acceptable). The secondary mirror (M2) and main aperture must handle a high-power launch beam of maximum 40W continuous wave at 1550 nm across the aperture or annulus (power density less than 3300 W per square metre on the primary mirror). Focusing Path and Clear Aperture: Must feature at least one Nasmyth focus port (more preferred). The Nasmyth focus path must be completely free of refracting optical elements (100 percent reflective optics only, with removable optics as an allowable deviation). Clear aperture path through the Nasmyth axis must be at least 60 mm diameter to support downstream Adaptive Optics relay systems. Mount and Dynamic Tracking Specifications: Alt-Azimuth Direct-Drive or equivalent performance mount with low-latency tracking dynamics supporting Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking, including high-elevation passes over Zenith. Minimum Azimuth Slew Rate must be at least 5 degrees per second (faster preferred). Pointing and tracking accuracy must be less than 8 to 10 arcsec RMS during dynamic LEO passes. Fastest tracking rate must exceed 1 degree per second with fine range control below this speed. Envelope and Enclosure Compatibility: Total vertical height must not exceed 3000 mm from the base to ensure dome clearance. Maximum radial swing clearance envelope must be at most 1470 mm. The axis of elevation pivot height must ensure clearance at all pointing directions, with the pivot axis positioned no more than 155 mm below the centre of the clearance envelope (or at the centre or higher). Full CAD models and opto-mechanical layout files are mandatory upon contract award. Software, Control Interface and API: Native integration with standard open-source astronomical communication protocols (INDI / INDIGO) or ASCOM / ALPACA frameworks. Open, fully documented network API adaptable to HTTP/REST or WebSocket interfaces for automated robotic control, telemetry, and scriptable trajectory loading. Ethernet data interface and DC power supply preferred. Delivery Constraint: Unit delivery must be completed within 3 to 4 months maximum from contract signature. This procurement is being undertaken as part of Phase 2 of Ireland's QCI project (TransEuroOGS), co-funded by the European Commission Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the Irish Department of Culture, Communications, and Sport. The successful tenderer will be required to design, manufacture, and deliver a turnkey telescope unit encompassing the mount, optics, and control software, complying with strict technical and spatial constraints. Key Technical Requirements: Optical Configuration: Ritchey-Chretien (RC) optical design, f/10 to f/12 system, with a clear aperture of at least 700 mm. Low central obstruction is required (30 percent or lower diameter linear obstruction preferred, maximum allowable 34 percent or lower). Optical Coatings and Power Handling: Broad-spectrum reflectivity covering both visible wavelengths and the 1550 nm C-Band NIR telecommunication spectrum, biased for optimal performance at 1550 nm. Reflectance at 1550 nm must be at least 95 percent (protected gold or equivalent high-efficiency NIR coating acceptable). The secondary mirror (M2) and main aperture must handle a high-power launch beam of maximum 40W continuous wave at 1550 nm across the aperture or annulus (power density less than 3300 W per square metre on the primary mirror). Focusing Path and Clear Aperture: Must feature at least one Nasmyth focus port (more preferred). The Nasmyth focus path must be completely free of refracting optical elements (100 percent reflective optics only, with removable optics as an allowable deviation). Clear aperture path through the Nasmyth axis must be at least 60 mm diameter to support downstream Adaptive Optics relay systems. Mount and Dynamic Tracking Specifications: Alt-Azimuth Direct-Drive or equivalent performance mount with low-latency tracking dynamics supporting Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking, including high-elevation passes over Zenith. Minimum Azimuth Slew Rate must be at least 5 degrees per second (faster preferred). Pointing and tracking accuracy must be less than 8 to 10 arcsec RMS during dynamic LEO passes. Fastest tracking rate must exceed 1 degree per second with fine range control below this speed. Envelope and Enclosure Compatibility: Total vertical height must not exceed 3000 mm from the base to ensure dome clearance. Maximum radial swing clearance envelope must be at most 1470 mm. The axis of elevation pivot height must ensure clearance at all pointing directions, with the pivot axis positioned no more than 155 mm below the centre of the clearance envelope (or at the centre or higher). Full CAD models and opto-mechanical layout files are mandatory upon contract award. Software, Control Interface and API: Native integration with standard open-source astronomical communication protocols (INDI / INDIGO) or ASCOM / ALPACA frameworks. Open, fully documented network API adaptable to HTTP/REST or WebSocket interfaces for automated robotic control, telemetry, and scriptable trajectory loading. Ethernet data interface and DC power supply preferred. Delivery Constraint: Unit delivery must be completed within 3 to 4 months maximum from contract signature. Please refer to the detailed Technical Specification document for full technical specifications, compliance matrices, and contractual terms.</cbc:Description>

                <cbc:ProcurementType languageID="ENG">This procurement acquires a specialized, highly innovative Optical Ground Station (OGS) telescope unit required for satellite-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) under the European Union EuroQCI initiative and the TransEuroOGS project.
The subject matter represents an innovative supply because it incorporates advanced technical and architectural capabilities that exceed conventional astronomical instrumentation:
Novel Optical and Power Handling: The system requires custom broad-spectrum optical coatings optimized at 1550 nm with reflectance of at least 95 percent, capable of withstanding high-power continuous-wave laser launch beams of up to 40W across the aperture for quantum and classical uplinks without thermal degradation.
Advanced Space-to-Ground Interface: It incorporates an unvignetted, completely reflective Nasmyth focus path (free of refracting glass optics) specifically engineered to interface directly with downstream Adaptive Optics systems and quantum photon receivers.
High-Dynamic Satellite Tracking: The mount features direct-drive mechanics engineered for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking across Zenith passes, achieving slew rates of at least 5 degrees per second and dynamic tracking pointing accuracy of 8 to 10 arcseconds RMS or better.
Open Robotic Control Architecture: The control system incorporates open network communication protocols and programmable APIs to integrate automated satellite tracking, real-time telemetry, and synchronization with European quantum satellite missions, notably Eagle-1.
This innovative equipment directly supports the deployment and cross-border validation of Europe's sovereign quantum communication infrastructure.</cbc:ProcurementType>

normalized.description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection. CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.

normalized.title: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems
normalized.description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection. CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.

normalized.title: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems
normalized.description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection. CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.

normalized.title: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems
normalized.description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection.  CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.
